Coordinate a publication-oriented research-direction investigation.

- Preserve the human's exact research goals from the attached source email.
- Delegate independent literature, browser/JavaScript systems, and feasibility investigations to multiple strongest available workers.
- Require at least one adversarial worker to challenge novelty, scope, and top-conference viability.
- Require broad personal-browser web searches using varied terms and search engines, Google Scholar paper exploration, and ChatGPT discussion as requested.
- Preserve relevant papers and compact notes outside the work-log repository.
- Synthesize a high-level report proposing concrete directions, prior art, novelty gaps, feasibility, evaluation plans, risks, and plausible prestigious venues.
- Have a fresh one-shot eval worker judge the final result against the human's goal before closure; if it fails, launch a new implementation worker and a new eval worker.
- Email the human directly with substantive updates and the final report; include `memory_research_mgr.md` in the subject.

You are the research submanager and must only route, track, and communicate; delegate all research and synthesis work. Keep high-level state in the task records and ensure all worker-owned artifacts have exactly one owner. Report to the upper manager only through a concise private `omo_report.sh` report using its allocated message file workflow.
(Adversarial interim: whole-browser memory comparisons do not support engine-level attribution; the defensible browser direction is a controlled same-macOS pressure, lifecycle, and process-topology study. Generic stack allocation, JS-to-Wasm conversion, and generic agentic memory optimization already show major novelty collisions. Allocation and transformation challenges remain in progress.)
(Adversarial workstream completed after an internal fix-and-rereview loop; the substantive memo was emailed to the human and preserved under /ssd1/sichangheagent/memadv/artifacts/. Search friction came from Google/Scholar authentication and CAPTCHA; primary repositories, Crossref, OpenAlex, and arXiv provided documented fallbacks. The browser-ChatGPT helper also needs more resilient model selection and a documented short-prompt fallback.)
(Browser/runtime workstream completed after independent review and a macOS-accounting correction; the substantive memo was emailed to the human and preserved under /ssd1/sichangheagent/membrowser/artifacts/. Primary-source snapshots improved claim discipline. Reproducibility was hindered by search authentication/CAPTCHA, a failing generic search connector, publisher access failures, and ChatGPT model-picker/connection failures; a browser-research exporter for query, URL, excerpt, timestamp, denominator, and completed model response would help.)
(Feasibility workstream completed after semantic-consistency fixes and independent review; the substantive memo and bounded experiments were emailed to the human and preserved under /ssd1/sichangheagent/memfeas/. The strongest surviving direction is verifier-checked, cross-engine packing of large long-lived homogeneous value-record collections, gated by a real-application candidate census and three-application manual-oracle study; TypedArrays are the primary backend and Wasm is an ablation. Search authentication/CAPTCHA, backend and Unicode failures, and ChatGPT timeout/shared-tab ambiguity suggest adding stable per-agent browser targets, resumable polling, and Unicode-safe extraction.)
(Literature/novelty workstream completed with a clean reviewer rerun; the substantive memo was emailed to the human and preserved under /ssd1/sichangheagent/memlit/. Vocabulary-driven searches initially missed the closest collision; an exact-mechanism ChatGPT pass plus exact-title and forward-citation checks corrected the memo. Future searches should include mechanism phrases such as runtime columnar array transformation in JavaScript early, and the ChatGPT helper should capture completion state reliably.)
